'''Kurt Gottfried''' (May 17, 1929 – August 25, 2022) was an Austrian-born American physicist who was [[professor emeritus]] of physics at [[Cornell University]]. He was known for his work in the areas of [[quantum mechanics]] and [[particle physics]] and was also a co-founder with [[Henry Way Kendall]] of the [[Union of Concerned Scientists]]. He wrote extensively in the areas of [[physics]] and [[arms control]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-12-01 |title=Kurt Gottfried 1929–2022 |url=https://cerncourier.com/a/kurt-gottfried-1929-2022/ |access-date=2023-03-16 |website=CERN Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Gottfried was born in [[Vienna]], First Austrian Republic, on May 17, 1929.<ref name="nyt">{{cite web|title=Kurt Gottfried, Physicist and Foe of Nuclear Weapons, Dies at 93|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/09/09/science/kurt-gottfried-dead.html|work=The New York Times|date=September 9, 2022|access-date=September 9, 2022}}</ref><ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=LzcgAQAAIAAJ&q=Kurt+Gottfried+17.+Mai+1929 Biografien österreichischer <nowiki>[</nowiki>Physiker<nowiki>]</nowiki><sup>innen</sup>: eine Auswahl]</ref> In 1939, after their home in Austria was raided on [[Kristallnacht]], his family emigrated to [[Montreal|Montreal, Quebec]], Canada.<ref name="Profile"/> Gottfried attended [[McGill University]], studying both [[Theoretical physics|theoretical]] and [[engineering physics]].<ref name="Weisskopf">{{cite book|editor-last1=Stefan|editor-first1=V.|title=Physics and society: essays in honor of Victor Frederick Weisskopf |date=1997|publisher=AIP Press|location=Woodbury, N.Y.|isbn=978-1563963865|page=124|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dlibDO1WFkUC&pg=PA124|access-date=March 24, 2016}}</ref><ref name="Jackson">{{cite journal|last1=Jackson|first1=J. David|title=Snapshots of a Physicist's Life|journal=[[Annual Review of Nuclear and Particle Science]]|date=December 1999|volume=49|issue=1|pages=1–33|doi=10.1146/annurev.nucl.49.1.1|bibcode = 1999ARNPS..49....1J |doi-access=free}}</ref>

Gottfried studied with [[Victor Weisskopf]] at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) from 1952 to 1955, completing his Ph.D. thesis, ''Investigations Based on the Bohr-Mottelson Nuclear Model''.<ref name="Weisskopf"/> There he studied deformed nuclei, developing models to describe wave functions and energy levels associated with nucleonic motion in a nonspherical force field, and comparing the results of those models to empirical data.<ref name="Gottfried1955">{{cite book|last1=Gottfried|first1=Kurt|title=Investigations Based on the Bohr-Mottelson Nuclear Model (Ph.D. Thesis)|date=1955|publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology|location=Cambridge, MA|bibcode=1955PhDT........13G}}</ref><ref name="Gottfried1956">{{cite journal|last1=Gottfried|first1=Kurt|title=Ground-State Properties of Nonspherical Nuclei|journal=Physical Review|date=August 15, 1956|volume=103|issue=4|pages=1017–1031|doi=10.1103/PhysRev.103.1017|url=http://inspirehep.net/record/45664/|access-date=March 25, 2016|bibcode = 1956PhRv..103.1017G |url-access=subscription}}</ref> His roommate at MIT was [[Henry Way Kendall|Henry Kendall]].<ref name="Profile"/>

== Career ==
Gottfried married Sorel Dickstein in 1955, whom he credits as being instrumental in the founding of the Union of Concerned Scientists and an invaluable collaborator over the course of his life.<ref>{{Citation|chapter=Students and Society |date=2019|title=March 4: Scientists, Students, and Society |publisher=The MIT Press |doi=10.7551/mitpress/11671.003.0007|isbn=978-0-262-35184-3|s2cid=214330860 |last1=Feigenbaum |first1=Joel |pages=3–8 }}</ref><ref name="Profile">{{cite journal|title=[MEMBER PROFILE] The Original Concerned Scientist: Kurt Gottfried|journal=Catalyst|date=2015|volume=Fall|url=http://www.ucsusa.org/publications/catalyst/fa15-member-profile.html|access-date=March 24, 2016}}</ref><ref name="MaidenName">{{cite news|title=Montreal Jewry mourns communal leader|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=883&dat=19560302&id=V-5OAAAAIBAJ&pg=5814,809703&hl=en|access-date=March 31, 2016|work=The Canadian Jewish Chronicle|date=March 2, 1956}}</ref> He then held short-term academic positions at [[Harvard University]] (1955–1958), [[CERN]], the [[Niels Bohr Institute]], and again at Harvard (1961–1964) before accepting a position in the physics department at [[Cornell University]] in 1964.<ref name="Weisskopf"/>

Gottfried became an associate professor at Cornell in 1964, a professor in 1968, and professor emeritus in 1998.<ref name="Cornell">{{cite web |title=Kurt Gottfried Professor of Physics Emeritus|url=https://physics.cornell.edu/kurt-gottfried |website=Cornell University |access-date=September 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220329183725/https://physics.cornell.edu/kurt-gottfried |archive-date=March 29, 2022 |location=web.archive.org |url-status=dead}}</ref>  He was a visiting professor at MIT from 1968 to 1969, and took a leave of absence to work at CERN from 1970 to 1973.<ref name="Weisskopf"/>  He served as department chair of the physics department at Cornell University from 1991 to 1994.<ref name="Cornell"/>

He died on August 25, 2022, at the age of 93.<ref>[https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/name/kurt-gottfried-obituary?id=36358787 Dr. Kurt Gottfried], legacy.com</ref><ref name="Cornell-Obit">{{cite web |last1=Hovis |first1=Kathy |title=Eminent physicist Kurt Gottfried, co-founder of Union of Concerned Scientists, dies at 93 {{!}} Department of Physics |url=https://physics.cornell.edu/news/eminent-physicist-kurt-gottfried-co-founder-union-concerned-scientists-dies-93 |website=physics.cornell.edu |access-date=September 11, 2022 |language=en |date=September 8, 2022}}</ref>

== Research ==
Gottfried worked with [[John David Jackson (physicist)|J. David Jackson]] in the 1960s on the production and decay of unstable resonances in high-energy hadronic collisions.<ref>
{{cite journal
 |last1=Gottfried|first1=K.|last2= Jackson|first2= J. D.
 |s2cid=121279157|year=1964
 |title=On the connection between production mechanism and decay of resonances at high energy
 |journal=[[Nuovo Cimento]]
 |volume=33 |pages=309–330
 |doi=10.1007/BF02750195
 |issue=2
| bibcode=1964NCim...33..309G|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/345301}}</ref> They introduced the use of the [[density matrix]] to connect production mechanisms to the decay patterns and described the influence of competing processes ("absorption") on the reactions.<ref>
{{cite journal
 |last1=Gottfried|first1=K.|last2= Jackson|first2= J. D.
 |s2cid=35362627|year=1964
 |title=Influence of absorption due to competing processes on peripheral reactions
 |journal=[[Nuovo Cimento]]
 |volume=34 |pages=735–752
 |doi=10.1007/BF02750013
 |issue=3
| bibcode=1964NCim...34..735G|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/2221228}}</ref> Gottfried studied meson–nucleon reactions, high-energy electron–proton scattering and the spectroscopy of heavy-quark bound states; and proposed the [[Gottfried sum rule]] for [[deep inelastic scattering]] to test the elementary [[quark model]].<ref name="Watson">{{cite book|last1=Watson|first1=Andrew|title=The Quantum Quark|date=2008|publisher=Cambridge University Press|location=Cambridge, MA|isbn=9780521089838|page=337|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ip50x8IOfnEC&pg=PA337}}</ref><ref name="Sum1967">{{cite journal|last1=Gottfried|first1=Kurt|title=Sum Rule for High-Energy Electron-Proton Scattering|journal=Physical Review Letters|date=June 19, 1967|volume=18|issue=25|pages=1174–1177|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.18.1174|bibcode = 1967PhRvL..18.1174G }}<!-- |accessdate=26 March 2016 --></ref><ref name="Hafemeister">{{cite journal|last1=Hafemeister|first1=David|title=Life Views and Particle Physics|url=https://www.aps.org/units/fps/newsletters/2002/january/a4jan02.html|journal=APS Forum on Physics and Society|volume=31|year=2002|number=1}}</ref> Gottfried's ''Quantum Mechanics: Fundamentals'', originally published in 1966, is considered "one of the most used and respected accounts of quantum theory".<ref name="Whitaker"/>

Gottfried is known for his work in the 1970s on [[charmonium]], with [[Estia J. Eichten]], [[Toichiro Kinoshita]], [[Kenneth Lane (physicist)|Ken Lane]] and [[Tung-Mow Yan]].<ref>{{cite journal |author1=E. Eichten |author2=K. Gottfried |author3=T. Kinoshita |author4=J. Kogut |author5=K. D. Lane |author6=T.-M. Yan | title=Spectrum of Charmed Quark-Antiquark Bound States | journal=Physical Review Letters | volume=34 | pages=369–372 | year=1975 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.369 | bibcode=1975PhRvL..34..369E | issue=6}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=E. Eichten |author2=K. Gottfried |author3=T. Kinoshita |author4=K. D. Lane |author5=T.-M. Yan | title=Charmonium: The Model | journal=Physical Review | volume=D17 | pages=3090–3117 | year=1978 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.17.3090|bibcode = 1978PhRvD..17.3090E | issue=11 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author1=E. Eichten |author2=K. Gottfried |author3=T. Kinoshita |author4=K. D. Lane |author5=Tung-Mow Yan | title=Charmonium: Comparison With Experiment | journal=Physical Review | volume=D21 |issue=1 | pages=203–233 | year=1980 | doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.21.203|bibcode = 1980PhRvD..21..203E }}</ref>

Gottfried served as chair of the Division of Particles and Fields of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1981.<ref name="Cornell"/> With [[Victor Weisskopf]], he wrote ''Concepts of Particle Physics'' (1984), which was hailed as "An authoritative presentation of the basic concepts of particle physics by two internationally recognized leaders in the field."<ref name="OUP">{{cite web|title=Concepts of Particle Physics|url=http://www.oupcanada.com/catalog/9780195043730.html|website=Oxford University Press|access-date=March 26, 2016}}</ref>

''Quantum Mechanics: Fundamentals'' was one of the influences spurring [[John Stewart Bell]] to write his polemical "Against measurement" (1990). Since Bell's death, Gottfried has become one of his major commentators.<ref name="Whitaker"/><ref name="MaryBell">{{cite book|last1=Bell|first1=M.|last2=Gottfried|first2=K.|last3=Veltman|first3=M.|title=John S. Bell on the foundations of quantum mechanics|date=2001|publisher=World Scientific|location=Singapore|isbn=978-9810246884}}</ref>  The second edition of ''Quantum Mechanics: Fundamentals'', co-authored with Tung-Mow Yan, "is of exceptional interest, historical and otherwise".<ref name="Whitaker">{{cite journal|last1=Whitaker|first1=A|title=Quantum Mechanics: Fundamentals|journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General|date=February 27, 2004|volume=37|issue=8|pages=3073–3076|doi=10.1088/0305-4470/37/8/B01|bibcode = 2004JPhA...37.3073G }}</ref><ref name="Yan">{{cite book |author1=Kurt Gottfried |author2=Tung-Mow Yan | title = Quantum Mechanics: Fundamentals | edition=Second | publisher=Springer | series=Graduate Texts in Contemporary Physics | year=2004 |isbn = 978-0-387-22023-9}}</ref>

== Union of Concerned Scientists ==
He was a co-founder of the [[Union of Concerned Scientists]] (UCS).<ref name="Kendall">{{cite book|last1=Kendall|first1=Henry W.|title=A distant light : scientists and public policy|date=2000|publisher=Springer|location=New York|isbn=9780387988337|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tRwBCAAAQBAJ&pg=PA2|access-date=March 25, 2016}}</ref><ref name="Allen">{{cite book|editor-last1=Allen|editor-first1=Jonathan|title=March 4 : scientists, students and society|date=1970|publisher=MIT Press|location=Cambridge, Mass.}}</ref> The organization was first formed on March 4, 1969, when Gottfried, Kendall, and other faculty at MIT organized a "teach-in" during which regular research would stop, and students and faculty would examine the "misuse of scientific and technical knowledge" that "presents a major threat to the existence of mankind."<ref name="Allen"/><ref name="Balogh">{{cite book|last1=Balogh|first1=Brian|title=Chain Reaction : Expert Debate and Public Participation in American Commercial Nuclear Power, 1945–75|date=1993|publisher=Cambridge University Press|location=Cambridge|isbn=9780521457361|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MqlepSpgByYC&pg=PA272}}</ref> Concerns included the [[Vietnam War]], [[nuclear weapons]], and [[environmental issues]].<ref name="Kendall"/>

{{quote|We are immersed in one of the most significant revolutions in man's history. The force that drives this revolution is ... relentless exploitations of scientific knowledge. That many of the transformations [from this revolution] have been immeasurably beneficial goes without saying. But, as with all revolutions, the technological revolution has released destructive forces and our society has failed to cope with them.|Kurt Gottfried, March 4, 1969<ref name="Profile"/>}}

Gottfried served on the board of directors of the UCS since 1978<ref name="Weisskopf"/> and as its vice-chairman<ref name="Weisskopf"/> and chairman (1999–2009).<ref name="USCBio">{{cite web|title=About Kurt Gottfried|url=https://www.ucsusa.org/about/kurt-gottfried.html|website=Union of Concerned Scientists|access-date=March 25, 2016}}</ref><ref name="Gold2007">{{cite news|last1=Gold|first1=Lauren|title=Salpeter and Gottfried sign letter urging Congress to pass binding resolution against nuclear weapons|url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2007/02/scientists-push-binding-resolution-against-nuclear-weapons|access-date=March 25, 2016|work=Cornell Chronicle|date=February 13, 2007}}</ref> Issues of particular concern to Gottfried are nuclear arms control,<ref name="Weisskopf"/> scientific integrity in the face of government pressure,<ref name="Profile"/> and human rights.<ref name="Weisskopf"/>

In 1982, Gottfried and [[Hans Bethe]] drafted a letter to [[Leonid Brezhnev]] protesting the Soviet treatment of peace activists in the Soviet Union.<ref name="BAS1982">{{cite journal|title=Arms control advocates protest harassment of Soviet peace group|journal=Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists|date=Nov 1982|pages=62–63|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dQoAAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA62|access-date=March 25, 2016}}</ref> As a member of the executive committee of SOS (Scientists For Sakharov, Orlov, and Shcharansky)<ref name="OAC">{{cite web|title=Collection Guide to Register of the Scientists For Sakharov, Orlov and Shcharansky Records, 1975–2010|url=https://www.oac.cdlib.org/findaid/ark:/13030/tf658004rz|website=Online Archive of California|access-date=March 26, 2016}}</ref>
Gottfried helped lead successful efforts to bring dissident scientist [[Yuri Orlov]] out of exile in Siberia, and offer him a position at Cornell,<ref name="Orlov">{{cite news|title=OFFER TO ORLOV OPEN|url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/1986-10-09/news/8603010710_1_amy-carter-train-station-beatle|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151210174743/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/1986-10-09/news/8603010710_1_amy-carter-train-station-beatle|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 10, 2015|access-date=March 25, 2016|work=Sun Sentinel|date=October 9, 1986}}</ref><ref name="Gazette1986">{{cite news|title=Soviet dissident Orlov takes Cornell position|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1917&dat=19861222&id=uBUhAAAAIBAJ&pg=5625,7299021&hl=en|access-date=March 25, 2016|work=Schenectady Gazette|issue=10|date=December 24, 1986}}</ref> which Orlov accepted.<ref name="Gold2005">{{cite news|last1=Gold|first1=Lauren|title=First Andrei Sakharov Prize for human rights goes to Cornell physicist and former Soviet gulag prisoner Yuri Orlov|url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2005/11/yuri-orlov-recognized-his-commitment-human-rights|work=Cornell Chronicle|date=November 14, 2005}}</ref>

Gottfried, Kendall, Hans Bethe, [[Richard Garwin]], and others strongly critiqued the U.S. [[Strategic Defense Initiative|"Star Wars" missile defense program]].<ref name="Reagan">{{cite news|title=Reagan's Star Wars|url=https://www.nybooks.com/articles/1984/04/26/reagans-star-wars/|access-date=March 25, 2016|work=New York Review of Books|date=April 26, 1984}}</ref>  Gottfried also co-edited ''[[Crisis Stability And Nuclear War]]'' (1988).<ref name="Gottfried1988">{{cite book|editor-last1=Gottfried|editor-first1=Kurt|editor-last2=Blair|editor-first2=Bruce G.|title=Crisis stability and nuclear war|url=https://archive.org/details/isbn_9780195051476|url-access=registration|date=1988|publisher=Oxford University Press|location=New York|isbn=978-0195051476}}</ref> The American Academy of Arts and Sciences cooperated with Cornell University's Peace Studies Program to sponsor a study on nuclear weapons and the command and control systems of the United States and the Soviet Union.<ref name="Solomon">{{cite book|last1=Solomon|first1=Fredric|last2=Marston|first2=Robert Q.|title=Medical Implications of Nuclear War|date=1986|publisher=National Academies Press|location=Washington, D.C.|isbn=9780309036924|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NUUrAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA5}}</ref> Gottfried and [[Bruce G. Blair]] edited the resulting book, representing the thinking of fifteen leading analysts.<ref name="Taylor">{{cite book|last1=Taylor|first1=Brendan|last2=Farrely|first2=Nicholas|last3=Lee|first3=Sheryn|title=Insurgent intellectual : essays in honour of Professor Desmond Ball|date=2012|publisher=Institute of Southeast Asian Studies|location=Singapore|isbn=978-981-4414-62-3|page=62|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ivZD01SoiDsC&pg=PA232}}</ref>

In 2004, Gottfried drafted the UCS statement ''Restoring Scientific Integrity in Policy Making'', which criticized the [[George W. Bush|Bush administration]] and called for "restoration of scientific integrity in the United States".<ref name="USCBio"/>  It was released on February 18, 2004, and supported by two UCS reports: ''[[Scientific Integrity in Policymaking|Scientific Integrity in Policy Making: An Investigation into the Bush Administration's Misuse of Science]]'' and ''Scientific Integrity in Policy Making: Further investigation of the Bush administration's abuse of science''.<ref name="UCS2004">{{cite web|title=Scientific Integrity in Policy Making (2004)|url=https://www.ucsusa.org/our-work/center-science-and-democracy/promoting-scientific-integrity/reports-scientific-integrity.html|website=Union of Concerned Scientists|access-date=March 25, 2016}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Gottfried was a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]. He received the 1992 [[Leo Szilard Lectureship Award|Leo Szilard Award]].<ref name="APSAward">{{cite web|title=Forum on Physics and Society: Leo Szilard Lectureship Award|url=https://www.aps.org/units/fps/awards/szilard.cfm|website=American Physical Society|access-date=March 25, 2016}}</ref> He was also a member of the Council of Foreign Relations.<ref name=Council>{{cite web|title=Why does Council on Foreign Relations keep popping up?|url=http://www.democraticunderground.com/discuss/duboard.php?az=view_all&address=203x278766|website=Democratic Underground}}</ref>
